info.name: ZifIQ Backend API
info.description: Test collection for the ZifIQ Kotlin/Spring Boot backend: every module with real persistence and business logic (Auth, Tenants & Members, OTP, VAT Control, Settings, Factory, Inventory, NRS Reference Data, Customers, Documents & Files, Showroom, Finance & Accounting, Electronic Invoicing, Sales & POS, Audit & Compliance). Modules still returning mock data (AI, Barcode, Process Guide) are left out until they are built. Run the folders top to bottom, 01 through 20: each request's Tests script captures IDs and tokens into collection variables that later requests reuse, so the whole collection runs end to end in the Collection Runner or Newman with no manual edits. See docs/ in the backend repo for the design each module implements.

request.description: Self-service root-tenant bootstrap. Run this first -- every other request depends on the token/tenant/credentials it creates. The email uses Postman's {{$guid}} dynamic variable so re-running this request never collides with a previous run's account -- no need to reset the database between test passes. Every later request that needs these credentials (Login, Forgot Password) reads them back from the registeredEmail/registeredPassword variables this sets, instead of a hardcoded literal, so they never drift out of sync.

request.description: multipart/form-data, part `file`: PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF or SVG of at most 1 MB, stored in S3 (purpose settings.company-logo). The type is checked from the file's content, not its name; an SVG with script, event handlers, foreignObject, a DOCTYPE or links to other files is refused (400 FILE_UNSAFE). The profile's logoUrl is a short-lived (1 h) S3 link that shows the image in place — use it as an , and read the profile again for a fresh one. logoInDocuments is false for AVIF and WebP, which the PDF engine can't draw: invoices and receipts then print the trading name. DELETE on the same path removes the logo (perm settings.manage). Newman uses postman/fixtures/company-logo.png.

exec: pm.test('logo is set and linked from storage', () => { pm.expect(json.data.hasLogo).to.eql(true); pm.expect(json.data.logoUrl).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(json.data.logoContentType).to.eql('image/png'); });
pm.test('response has data envelope', () => { const j = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(j).to.have.property('data'); });

item.description:
Customers & Distributors (backend docs/04). Needs 01 - Auth > Register Tenant first (for the token); everything else this folder needs it creates itself, so it can be run on its own right after Register Tenant.

Run top to bottom - requests are lettered by area and each one sets up the next:
A setup (a home location) - B dealer categories - C correspondents - D registering customers of every type - E search, filters and pickers - F wallet/deposit ledger, adjustments, reversals - G promotion/demotion - H status - I rules that span records - J dealer self-service.

Requests marked "(error: ...)" deliberately break a business rule and assert the exact error code, so a full run is all green. Captured variables: customerLocationId, today, goldCategoryId, diamondCategoryId, correspondentId, correspondent2Id, dealerId, dealerName, dealerCode, customerId, specialId, walkinId, adjustmentEntryId, reclassificationId.

request.description: Perm showroom.returns.manage; the showroom must be ACTIVE. No customer record? Give walkIn {name, phone}: an existing non-dealer with that phone is used, otherwise a temporary customer is created (removed once its wallet is spent). Every line is credited to the wallet at today's price (retail for non-dealers, dealer price for dealers; 400 PRICE_NOT_SET if none). RESALEABLE goes back into stock (receiving area), QUARANTINE into the quarantine area (created on first use, never sold from), DAMAGED_WRITE_OFF is recorded as a loss.

request.description: Perm invoicing.invoice.read; location-scoped (a single-location user never sees another showroom's invoices). status takes DRAFT, ISSUED, PARTIALLY_PAID, PAID, OVERDUE, VOID. The derived ones are computed in SQL from payments, credit notes, the due date and invoicing.paidTolerance, so they filter, facet and sort like stored columns. Other filters: customerId, customerType, locationId, sourceType, invoiceKind, issueDate/dueDate (from, to, period), total, paid, balance, daysOverdue, issuedBy, correspondentId, vatEnabled, hasWaybills, hasReplacement. q matches the number (a bare 4031 finds INV-4031), the source/pro-forma reference, buyer name, phone, TIN or e-mail. Sort issuedAt (default, newest first), number, total, balance, dueDate, daysOverdue, buyerName.
